subject: history
title: Revolutions: Cause and Effect
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace what caused each revolution and what changed afterwards.
meta_desc: GCSE History Revolutions causes and consequences — American, French, Russian.
final_note: You can now explain the causes and consequences of each of the three revolutions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
After 1763 Britain taxed the colonies to pay for war debts.

The Stamp Act, Tea Act and Boston Massacre fed resentment. By 1775 fighting broke out at Lexington. The result was a new republic with a written Constitution by 1787.

France's three Estates were unequal — clergy and nobles paid no tax. Bread prices soared in 1788-89.

The Bastille fell on 14 July 1789. The Declaration of the Rights of Man followed. But the Reign of Terror under Robespierre showed revolution can devour its own.

Tsar Nicholas II refused real reform after 1905. WWI brought military disaster and food shortages.

The February 1917 revolution made a weak Provisional Government. It kept fighting Germany — fatal. Lenin's promise of 'Peace, Bread, Land' won support and the Bolsheviks seized power in October.
